newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks up two percent in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks up two percent in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices extended early gains to rise sharply in late Wednesday trade as bullish sentiment overtook the anxieties that triggered Tuesday's correction, brokers said.
The index rallied despite the watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission's public statement urging 20 local securities investment trust firms not to manipulate stocks.
With 18 minutes of trading to go, the index was up 169.32 points or 2.00 percent 8,629.95.
Turnover was a very hectic T$170 billion.
"Initially, investors were worried that Tuesday's fall on record (T$238.9 billion) turnover indicated heavy profit-taking was emerging," said Alex Chen of HSBC James Capel.

"But as the market now has far more listed firms, more new local mutual funds have been set up and foreign funds have been allowed in, investors should get used to a daily turnover above T$200 billion," Chen said.
Financials and plastics, which lagged recent gains, emerged to lead the rise, surging 3.27 percent and 3.66 percent, respectively. Electronics, the recent gainers, were mixed.
